title: The LCR Bench
summary: Combine R, L and C in series with phasors: impedance, current, phase and voltages that do not add up.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 7.6, AC voltage applied to a series LCR circuit
learningOutcome: The student can find the impedance, current and phase of series RC, RL and LCR circuits, and add voltages as phasors instead of arithmetically.

levels.title: Resistor and capacitor
levels.adds: Baseline: in a series RC circuit Z = √(R² + X_C²), and V_R + V_C exceeds the source voltage (Example 7.6).
hints: Then I = V/Z and V_C = I X_C.

levels.title: Series LCR
levels.adds: New idea: Z = √(R² + (X_L − X_C)²) and tan φ = (X_L − X_C)/R (Example 7.8).
hints: Subtract X_C from X_L before squaring.
If X_L is bigger the current lags; if X_C is bigger it leads.

levels.title: Add the phasors
levels.adds: More steps: the three voltages add as phasors: V = √(V_R² + (V_L − V_C)²) (Section 7.6.1).
hints: V_L and V_C are opposite in phase, so subtract them.
V_R is a quarter cycle from the difference.

levels.title: A real coil
levels.adds: Apply it: a coil is a resistor in series with an inductor, with power factor R/Z (Section 7.7).
hints: The power factor is cos φ = R/Z.

misconceptions: Impedance is the sum R + X_L + X_C
The voltages across R, L and C add up arithmetically to the source voltage
The reactances of L and C add
